data.narrative:
Lace Lithography is a Series A–stage semiconductor company that has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private-stage peers in Chips & Semiconductors, including Rebellions, d-Matrix, and Positron AI.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, anchoring to the $60M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement, implies a valuation of $120M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—Rebellions ($2.3B), d-Matrix ($2.0B), and Positron AI ($1.0B)—yields a median valuation of $2.0B, with a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (median 20.4x across the three public tickers) is not applicable due to absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies. Synthesizing these results produces a triangulated range of $102M (low) to $2.3B (high), with a median of $1.1B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around whether stage-based progression or peer multiples better reflect Lace's position within the frontier-semiconductor landscape, as well as unknowns regarding technology differentiation, capital efficiency, and path to revenue relative to established peers.
